title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic likeness of a named public figure, in this case a sitting Chief Minister, delivered over a live WhatsApp video call. The deepfake was only the opening move. The rest of the fraud ran on fabricated paperwork, a supposed manager, a supposed CBI officer, and a sequence of fee demands that moved the victim from belief to payment. The synthetic face did the work of establishing authority that the callers did not have.

The failure sits at the point where a consumer messaging platform carries a real-time video call with no verification that the person on screen is who they claim to be. Nothing in the account shows any check between the claim of office and the demand for money. Catching it would have required confirming the caller through an official channel independent of the call itself, or a verification step at the payment, and neither existed here. The victim's own refusal of a further demand, and his later contact with the cybercrime helpline and Byappanahalli police, is where the chain stopped.

What is not established is who generated the deepfake, whether the callers had any connection to the offices they invoked, and what the registered case under the Information Technology Act will find. The account rests on a single outlet's report, and a registered case is not a verdict.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, lost more than Rs 1.04 lakh after a WhatsApp video call used a deepfake of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. On Sept 9, the caller claimed to be Vijay and offered Rs 11 lakh in aid, saying the money would come through a foreign account in dollars. A supposed manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for fees, including Rs 5,000 for exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN. Another person posing as a CBI official demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri made several digital payments before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand.

Giri then contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and approached Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. The fraudsters had sent him a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh was allotted and identity proof said to belong to a CBI officer. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims. This was the first such case reported in the city.
